annotations.title: The idols of the Gentiles are ſiluer and gold.
annotations.text: Al Catholique Diuines agree in this authentical definition, of Idolatrie, <mn>[1]</mn> that it is diuine honour geuen to anie creature, as to a god. Of the diuers ſortes alſo of Idolatrie the ancient lerned Doctors haue vvritten much. <mn>[2]</mn> Namely Iuſtinus Martyr in his Orations againſt the Gentiles, Tertullian in Apologetico, Arnobius Orat. ad Gentes. Lactantius, li. 1. c. 17. Diuinar. Inſtit. and manie others. But moſt copiouſly and profoundly S. Auguſtin, eſpecially in his tenne firſt bookes de Ciuitate Dei. Into which error & crime the Platoniſtes fel, holding that ſpiritual inuiſible created ſubſtances, to vvitte, Angels good and euil, <mn>[3]</mn> vvhom they called Intelligentias ſeparatas, had diuine powre, & ſo gaue to them diuine honour. Others honour dead men, and ſome before their death as goddes, for their notable actes atchieued in this life, as Saturne, Iuppiter, Hercules, and the like. Some yeld diuine honour to mere corporal creatures, <mn>[4]</mn> liuing or vvithout life, as to beaſtes and ſerpentes, the ſunne, the moone, fire, vvater, earth, the whole machin of the vvorld, as if it vvere animate, and that with diuine ſpirite or ſoule. Againe al theſe haue bene vvorſhipped as gods, <mn>[5]</mn> not only in them ſelues but alſo in their imagees. But to omite other diuerſities, the moſt groſſe ſorte of al, is the Idolatrie which the Pſalmiſt here deſcribeth, vvhen Imagees made by mens handes are immediatly honored as goddes in themſelues. <mn>[6]</mn> For ſuch goddes the Gentiles had, and of them the Prophet here ſpeaketh. Comparing theſe viſible ſenſles imagined goddes, <mn>[7]</mn>vvith the one eternal inuiſible God, who is made notorious by his diuine conſpicuous vvorkes, wheras theſe idols, by how much they are more viſible, ſo much more they are contemptible: becauſe being faſhioned vvith mouth, eyes, eares, noſe, handes, feete, throte, and other members, they are altogether ſenſles, not able to ſpeake vvith their mouth, and therin more baſe in nature, then the men that made them; nor able to ſee, heare, ſmel, taiſt, feele, to vvalke, to moue, nor to crie, al which beaſtes can doe. And therfore thoſe that make them, or haue confidence in them (as the Prophet here ſignifieth that ſome haue. v. 16.) are moſt abſurde: becoming like to the ſame idols, in their vnderſtanding and internal cogitations, as theſe idols are voide of external ſenſe. <mn>[8]</mn> And al Idolaters are moſt vvicked, geuing diuine honour to anie creature, & are therin ſeruantes of diuels: <mn>[9]</mn> VVhether they immediatly honour diuels, as when ſorcerers and vvitches, making pact vvith the diuel, adore him, and he for the ſame doth ſome thing which they demand: or that they honour ſome other creature, vvherin by the diuels falſe perſuaſion, they thincke there is diuine powre. Both which vvaies diuels vſurpe Gods honour and therfore the ſame Prophet ſaide in an other <mn>[10]</mn> Pſalme: Al the goddes of Gentiles are diuels.

notes.text: Corporal creatures, sensible and without sense.
